<p>Table of Contents</p><a id="fn5ybqxt3s7y"></a><h1>PRD — Pixel-Fidelity Figma-to-Code Engine</h1><a id="6aot0khecrmh"></a><h3>Phase 1–3 (Deterministic Core) | Phase 4 (AI/Automation) deferred</h3><a id="jpruuob1ycdr"></a><h3>v7 — Final Contract-Reconciled All-Phases Implementation Specification | deterministic core + controlled AI escalation + visual/compositing + responsive/constraints contracts</h3><a id="fgvhi47hkcbe"></a><h2>Architecture diagram</h2><p><img alt="Phase 1-3 deterministic architecture with Phase 4 AI deferred" src="data:image/png;base64," /></p><p><em>Phase 1-3 deterministic architecture with Phase 4 AI deferred</em></p><a id="n3j6a1x5krhw"></a><h2>1. Product framing</h2><p><strong>Not</strong>: a Figma-to-React generator. <strong>Is</strong>: a browser-verified visual reverse-engineering compiler that generates code and iteratively optimizes it against a real Chromium render, measured against the original Figma design.</p><p><strong>Lock-in rule #1</strong>:</p><p>The engine must never assume that Figma geometry directly equals CSS implementation. It must preserve observed geometry, infer implementation intent, evaluate the implementation in Chromium, and accept only validated improvements.</p><p><strong>Lock-in rule #2</strong>:</p><p>Every optimization is reversible, measurable, scoped, and reproducible.</p><p><strong>“Solid” definition</strong>: the engineering design is solid — deterministic, debuggable, measurable. Not a promise of 100% pixel-perfect output. Controlled benchmark target: <strong>95%+</strong>.</p><a id="qxl2fcye5nk9"></a><h2>2. Why AI is excluded from Phase 1–3</h2><p>Deliberate sequencing, not rejection:</p><table><thead><tr><th><p>Reason</p></th><th><p>Explanation</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Clean baseline</p></th><th><p>Must know what the deterministic engine achieves alone before mixing in AI’s contribution.</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Determinism</p></th><th><p>90%→95% must be repeatable and measurable. AI adds noise.</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Cost/latency</p></th><th><p>50–100 diff regions per page; sequential AI calls make the loop slow and expensive.</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Own architecture</p></th><th><p>rules → candidate search → AI escalation (last resort), never the reverse.</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Real moat</p></th><th><p>The engine (IR, solver, comparator, optimizer) is the product, not an LLM wrapper.</p></th></tr></thead></table><p>Exit criteria to unlock Phase 4: deterministic pipeline consistently hits ≥93–95% fidelity on the benchmark set. AI is then scoped narrowly to unresolved cases only (see §9 taxonomy) — never full-page generation.</p><a id="dwtakcadhooh"></a><h2>3. Success metrics</h2><p>Fidelity and Robustness are tracked as <strong>two separate scores</strong> — never collapsed into one number.</p><table><thead><tr><th><p>Metric</p></th><th><p>Phase 1 exit</p></th><th><p>Phase 2 exit</p></th><th><p>Phase 3 exit</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Fidelity score (static frame, primary breakpoint)</p></th><th><p>pipeline runs, score computed</p></th><th><p>≥ 90%</p></th><th><p>≥ 95%</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Robustness score (responsive/flow/dynamic content)</p></th><th><p>not required</p></th><th><p>not required</p></th><th><p>reported, no hard floor yet, tracked per §15.6 and validated per §17</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Determinism</p></th><th><p>environment-frozen, reproducible (see §14)</p></th><th><p>same</p></th><th><p>same</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Manual intervention</p></th><th><p>fully expected</p></th><th><p>rare</p></th><th><p>near zero on benchmark set</p></th></tr></thead></table><p><strong>Fidelity Score v1</strong> = configurable weighted composite of Geometry + Layout + Typography + Style + Assets + Perceptual visual diff. Weights are <strong>not</strong> frozen now — they are benchmark-calibrated before Phase 3 exit, based on which dimensions actually correlate with visual correctness on the real benchmark set. Example only, not final: Fidelity = 96.2%, Robustness = 91% reported side by side.</p><a id="n9vr2ptg7c90"></a><h2>4. Phase 1 — Deterministic Compiler</h2><p><strong>Goal</strong>: given one Figma frame, produce a real HTML/CSS render inside Chromium and get an honest, measured, reproducible score. Target here is <strong>pipeline correctness, not a high score</strong>.</p><p>Figma → Extractor → Parser → Design IR → HTML/CSS → Controlled Chromium<br />  → DOM metrics → Reference comparison → Score</p><a id="2h3nzux9qix4"></a><h3>4.1 Reference Rendering Contract (mandatory, per benchmark frame)</h3><p>Figma <em>geometry</em> and Figma <em>rendered pixels</em> are not the same thing. Before any comparison is trusted, freeze and record for every benchmark frame: - exact viewport width/height - exact export dimensions - device scale factor (DPR) - font environment (which fonts, which weights, source) - image assets used (exact files/hashes) - background (transparent vs. filled, and which color) - crop/export mode used to generate the reference image</p><p>The comparison engine consumes this contract as a fixed reference artifact — it does not re-derive it ad hoc per run.</p><a id="uxnjwd2f22ji"></a><h3>4.2 Persistent node identity (Phase 1, not Phase 4)</h3><p>Every NodeIR carries a stable identity from the very first parse, because Phase 2/3’s patch loop must re-recognize the same node across re-renders:</p><p><strong>interface</strong> NodeIdentity {<br />  figmaId: string;<br />  internalId: string;<br />  structureHash: string;<br />}</p><p>Identity reconciliation rule: figmaId remains the stable source identity and internalId remains the logical IR identity. structureHash is recomputed after every committed structural patch. A structural patch must emit an identity-reconciliation record mapping affected pre-patch nodes to post-patch nodes; unchanged logical nodes retain their internalId. If a logical node cannot be deterministically mapped, the patch is rejected or the case is emitted as UNRESOLVED_SOURCE_AMBIGUITY.</p><a id="lzucj99f9n20"></a><h3>4.3 Preserve component/instance identity now, infer abstraction later</h3><p>Phase 1 preserves Figma’s native component/instance metadata as-is on the IR node (which component, which instance, which variant) — it does <strong>not</strong> attempt reusable React abstraction. That inference is Phase 4 (Structure Intelligence). Preserving the metadata now avoids an IR schema rewrite later.</p><a id="dnbssqc27bee"></a><h3>4.4 Relative geometry from day one</h3><p>For every node, compute <strong>both</strong>: - absolute geometry - geometry relative to its immediate parent</p><p>Rule: use relative geometry for diagnosis, absolute geometry for final visual verification. Without this, a parent shifted +20px makes every descendant look independently wrong, and the optimizer chases the wrong target.</p><a id="tuuczakhubtu"></a><h3>4.5 Font/asset readiness precondition (non-optional)</h3><p>No screenshot is taken until all of the following are true: - document.fonts.ready resolved - all images loaded - network idle / asset readiness confirmed</p><p>Screenshot-before-ready is not an acceptable shortcut, even in early prototyping.</p><a id="bg9ar3gv1gze"></a><h3>Deliverables</h3><p>figma-parser, design-ir (with NodeIdentity, relative geometry, preserved component metadata), code-generator (plain HTML/CSS only), renderer (Playwright/Chromium wrapper, enforces readiness precondition), geometry-engine + visual-engine (comparison v1), reference-artifact store per §4.1.</p><a id="kl4a2blctbab"></a><h3>Exit criteria</h3><p>Pipeline runs end-to-end on 3 benchmark frames (simple/medium/complex) and returns a real, reproducible score — the number itself can be 60–75% at this stage.</p><a id="bjfhptabjrk"></a><h2>5. Phase 2 — Deterministic Optimizer (target: 90%)</h2><p>Diff → Relative geometry → Ancestor-first diagnosis → Rule patch<br />  → Same-browser evaluation → Commit / rollback</p><a id="wl3b1bxxwgha"></a><h3>5.1 Mutation boundaries (explicit allow-list)</h3><p>Canonical mutation authority: §16.4 is the normative mutation-boundary policy. This §5.1 table is a phase-level summary only; when rules differ, §16.4 governs.</p><table><thead><tr><th><p><strong>Allowed</strong></p></th><th><p>padding, gap, width, max-width, height, line-height</p></th></tr><tr><th><p><strong>Restricted</strong> (needs strong evidence)</p></th><th><p>layout mode, component boundary, DOM structure, content, asset source</p></th></tr><tr><th><p><strong>Forbidden by default</strong></p></th><th><p>random absolute positioning, arbitrary transforms, full-tree rewrites</p></th></tr></thead></table><p>Rule: a patch must mutate the <strong>smallest possible ancestor/subtree</strong> that explains the diff.</p><a id="20lh6haoomn2"></a><h3>5.2 Patch-based rollback (not full snapshots)</h3><p>Do not snapshot the entire project per candidate. Store per patch: - forward patch - reverse patch - parent version reference - score before - score after</p><p>This keeps memory/IO bounded as the loop iterates.</p><a id="g2sov0q69qbk"></a><h3>5.3 Chromium reuse contract</h3><p>Browser lifecycle:<br />  1 browser process<br />  1 reusable context<br />  N candidate evaluations</p><p>Candidate isolation is mandatory: each candidate must start from the same committed version and must not inherit prior candidate state. CSS overrides are applied and reset; cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, Cache Storage, service workers, permissions, and other mutable browser state must be cleared, blocked, or recreated according to the benchmark runtime policy. Candidate B must never inherit Candidate A state. Any state reset failure invalidates the candidate evaluation.</p><a id="tw1t0aahzh2"></a><h3>Deliverables</h3><p>root-cause-engine (diff → node → parent → ancestors, using relative geometry), optimizer (rule-based, enforces mutation boundaries), patch-engine (apply/measure/commit/rollback per §5.2), regression log of every patch attempt.</p><a id="onyitt163c9f"></a><h3>Exit criteria</h3><p>≥ 90% average fidelity score across the full benchmark set, zero manual code edits between runs.</p><a id="jljch1g24zgw"></a><h2>6. Phase 3 — Search + Responsive (target: 95%+)</h2><p>Worst subtree → Candidate generation → Cheap DOM filter → Beam search<br />  → Visual evaluation → Best candidate → Responsive stress</p><a id="trtro5ecwvcr"></a><h3>6.1 Type-specific candidate generation (not random CSS mutation)</h3><table><thead><tr><th><p>Ambiguity type</p></th><th><p>Candidates</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Width</p></th><th><p>fixed px / 100% + max-width / flex-based</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Gap</p></th><th><p>measured value ± nearby values</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Alignment</p></th><th><p>start / center / end / stretch</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Height</p></th><th><p>auto / fixed / min-height / aspect-ratio</p></th></tr></thead></table><p>Rule: mutate <strong>one hypothesis dimension at a time</strong> unless a rule explicitly defines a coupled change. This keeps the search space bounded and diagnosable.</p><a id="eteuj6ioq1w0"></a><h3>6.2 “Best version always survives” contract (mandatory)</h3><p>initialVersion = bestVersion<br />for every candidate:<br />    evaluate fidelity and robustness<br />    if candidate passes §15.5 acceptance gate:<br />        if candidate ranks better than best eligible version:<br />            bestVersion = candidate<br />return globally best observed eligible version</p><p>Optimization must never return an ineligible candidate. “Best” means best among eligible versions under §15.5: score improvement threshold, no critical regression, valid candidate, readiness-gated render. Fidelity ranks first, Robustness breaks Fidelity ties, then patch count and deterministic patch-ID tie-breakers apply as defined in §16.6.</p><a id="h5q8tct6af5w"></a><h3>6.3 Responsive correctness — expanded definition</h3><p>“No overflow” alone is insufficient; a page can pass that check and still be visually wrong. Responsive correctness must check: - overflow - collision - unexpected text wrap - unexpected component displacement - container instability - horizontal scroll - broken aspect ratio</p><p>Validated at 390 / 640 / 768 / 1024 / 1280 / 1440.</p><a id="g18o9t1b3gp2"></a><h3>6.4 Dynamic content stress test — guardrail</h3><p>Short/normal/long content injection may surface fixes like overflow: hidden or text-overflow: ellipsis. These are only acceptable when there is design evidence for them.</p><p>Rule: <strong>stress-test fixes must not override inferred/reference design intent without explicit evidence.</strong> A fix that merely hides overflow to “pass” the test, without matching how the design was actually meant to behave, is rejected.</p><a id="nglt5xk2dufx"></a><h3>Deliverables</h3><p>layout-solver (type-specific candidate generator + evaluator per §6.1), optimizer extended with beam search (width 2–3) + caching (DesignHash, IRHash, Viewport, DPR, FontHash), responsive-engine + flow-engine (expanded checks per §6.3), benchmark report per frame per breakpoint, best-version guarantee per §6.2.</p><a id="q6ohemncslzq"></a><h3>Exit criteria</h3><p>≥ 95% average fidelity score at the primary breakpoint, and no unresolved instances of the §6.3 failure list across 390–1440px on at least the simple and medium benchmark frames.</p><a id="ua1unun8jnv8"></a><h2>7. Phase 4 — AI (reference only, not started)</h2><p>Unresolved cases → AI<br />  ├── intent inference<br />  ├── composition<br />  ├── root-cause reasoning<br />  └── structured patch proposals<br />→ Structure Intelligence → React → Tailwind → Production cleanup</p><p>AI consumes the unresolved case log (see §9 taxonomy) built up during Phase 2/3 — this becomes its trigger/training dataset, which is why the taxonomy is defined now rather than retrofitted later. Model-agnostic by design: engine value doesn’t depend on which LLM is plugged in.</p><a id="6i3mcrd5pvim"></a><h2>8. Determinism — hardened definition</h2><p>“Same input → same output” is only true if the environment is frozen. Determinism requires <strong>all</strong> of: - source (Figma file/frame version) - browser version - viewport - DPR - font files - assets - generator version - rule version - benchmark configuration</p><p>→ same output. Any of these drifting invalidates a reproducibility claim.</p><a id="k1ssrs79zsrb"></a><h2>9. Unresolved case taxonomy (defined from Phase 2 onward)</h2><p>Every case the rule optimizer / candidate search cannot resolve is logged under one of:</p><p>UNRESOLVED_LAYOUT<br />UNRESOLVED_TYPOGRAPHY<br />UNRESOLVED_ASSET<br />UNRESOLVED_RENDERING<br />UNRESOLVED_RESPONSIVE<br />UNRESOLVED_MAPPING<br />UNRESOLVED_SOURCE_AMBIGUITY</p><p>This taxonomy is the handoff contract to Phase 4 — it defines exactly what AI is being asked to solve, rather than “whatever the pipeline couldn’t do.”</p><p>Canonical mapping from the granular Phase 2/3 root-cause classes to these seven handoff buckets is defined in §16.1A and is normative for logging and AI routing.</p><a id="u7poxmcan0mn"></a><h2>10. Minimal project structure for Phase 1–3</h2><p>figma-to-code/<br />├── apps/<br />│   └── cli/                  # simple CLI/script runner for now, web UI later<br />├── packages/<br />│   ├── figma-client/<br />│   ├── figma-parser/<br />│   ├── design-ir/             # NodeIdentity, relative geometry, component metadata preserved<br />│   ├── layout-solver/         # Phase 3<br />│   ├── paint-engine/            # Phase 1–3 visual normalization<br />│   ├── compositing-engine/      # Phase 1–3 opacity/blend/blur<br />│   ├── clipping-engine/         # Phase 1–3 clip/mask<br />│   ├── stacking-engine/         # Phase 1–3 stacking/z-index/paint order<br />│   ├── effect-engine/           # Phase 1–3 CSS/SVG effect mapping<br />│   ├── code-generator/        # HTML/CSS/SVG through phase 3<br />│   ├── renderer/              # Playwright/Chromium wrapper, readiness precondition enforced<br />│   ├── geometry-engine/<br />│   ├── visual-engine/<br />│   ├── root-cause-engine/     # Phase 2<br />│   ├── optimizer/             # rules (P2) -&gt; + candidate search (P3)<br />│   ├── patch-engine/          # Phase 2, patch-based rollback<br />│   ├── responsive-engine/     # Phase 3<br />│   ├── flow-engine/           # Phase 3<br />│   └── font-engine/<br />└── benchmark/<br />    ├── frames/                 # simple / medium / complex test frames<br />    ├── reference-artifacts/    # per Reference Rendering Contract, §4.1<br />    └── reports/                # scored results per run, unresolved-case log</p><p>No ai-agent, component-engine, structure-engine, or apps/web yet — those are Phase 4.</p><a id="vhojc0n1tbr7"></a><h2>11. First working prototype (concrete first milestone)</h2><ol><li>Input: one Figma frame, 1440×900 — reference contract captured per §4.1</li><li>Output: HTML/CSS (Phase 1 compiler)</li><li>Chromium screenshot, only after font/asset readiness (§4.5)</li><li>Geometry diff (relative + absolute, §4.4) + overlay</li><li>Score</li><li>Automatic padding/width/gap corrections within mutation boundaries (§5.1)</li><li>Target: 90%+ on this one frame before touching Phase 3</li></ol><p>Do not touch React, Tailwind, AI, or component abstraction until this milestone is passed.</p><a id="krhluydl9gfi"></a><h2>12. Development order (condensed)</h2><p>Phase 1: Parser → Design IR (identity + relative geometry + component metadata)<br />         → Basic Compiler → Chromium Runtime (readiness-gated) → Comparison v1<br />Phase 2: Root-Cause Engine (relative-geometry-based) → Rule Optimizer (bounded mutations)<br />         → Patch/Rollback loop (patch-based, not snapshot-based)             [target 90%]<br />Phase 3: Layout Solver (type-specific candidates, one dimension at a time)<br />         → Pruning/Beam/Cache → Best-version contract<br />         → Responsive Validation (expanded checks) → Dynamic Content stress  [target 95%]<br />Phase 4: AI escalation (consumes unresolved taxonomy) → Structure Intelligence<br />         → React/Tailwind → Production cleanup<br />         [NOT STARTED — reference only]</p><p><strong>12A. Phase 4 — Strong AI Architecture</strong></p><p><strong>Purpose. </strong>AI is a controlled escalation layer, not the primary renderer. The deterministic compiler, Chromium renderer, comparator, optimizer, and rollback system remain authoritative. AI proposes interpretations and patches; browser measurement decides acceptance.</p><p><strong>12A.1 Model strategy</strong></p><p>• Gemini: primary multimodal analyzer for screenshots, assets, OCR, and large visual context.</p><p>• OpenAI: complex layout reasoning, structured patch proposals, and difficult code-generation cases.</p><p>• Claude: code review, cleanup, refactoring, and visual-difference explanation.</p><p>• Groq: optional low-latency inference layer; quality depends on the vision model selected through it.</p><p>• The router must not call every model by default; escalate only when deterministic rules fail.</p><p><strong>12A.2 AI routing</strong></p><p>• UNRESOLVED_LAYOUT → Gemini, then OpenAI if confidence is low.</p><p>• UNRESOLVED_TYPOGRAPHY → OpenAI or Claude.</p><p>• UNRESOLVED_ASSET → Gemini.</p><p>• UNRESOLVED_RESPONSIVE → OpenAI, followed by multi-breakpoint browser validation.</p><p>• UNRESOLVED_MAPPING → Claude or OpenAI.</p><p>• UNRESOLVED_RENDERING → deterministic diagnosis first; AI only for explanation or a narrow hypothesis.</p><p>• UNRESOLVED_SOURCE_AMBIGUITY → human review by default; AI may propose evidence-backed interpretations, but no structural or semantic patch may be committed without explicit source evidence and deterministic validation.</p><p><strong>12A.3 Structured patch contract</strong></p><p>AI must return validated JSON and minimal patches, never an uncontrolled full-tree rewrite. Each proposal contains target node identity, property, old value, new value, reason, evidence, confidence, expected effect, and alternatives.</p><p>{<br />  "targetNode": "hero-content",<br />  "property": "gap",<br />  "oldValue": "16px",<br />  "newValue": "24px",<br />  "reason": "Heading-to-paragraph spacing is smaller than the reference",<br />  "confidence": 0.91<br />}</p><p><strong>12A.4 Acceptance and rollback</strong></p><p>1. Validate every response against JSON Schema or Zod.</p><p>2. Apply the smallest patch to the identified node or ancestor.</p><p>3. Render only after fonts, images, and network assets are ready.</p><p>4. Measure fidelity and robustness before and after the patch.</p><p>5. Commit only when the relevant score improves without responsive regressions.</p><p>6. Rollback automatically when the score decreases, a regression occurs, or output is invalid.</p><p><strong>12A.5 Confidence, disagreement, and caching</strong></p><p>Determinism boundary: Phase 4 AI proposal generation is potentially non-deterministic, even when the environment and inputs are frozen. Caching and versioning make accepted/cached proposals reproducible; they do not imply first-call model determinism. Only the post-proposal acceptance, validation, scoring, rollback, and release pipeline inherits the deterministic contract.</p><p>• Record confidence and evidence for every AI inference.</p><p>• For high-impact decisions, obtain independent proposals from two models and test both as candidates.</p><p>• Cache by source hash, frame hash, viewport, DPR, font hash, asset hash, prompt version, and model version.</p><p>• Version prompts, schemas, adapters, and model configuration as production artifacts.</p><p>• Send low-confidence or repeatedly failing cases to a human-review queue.</p><p><strong>12A.6 New packages</strong></p><p>• ai-router/</p><p>• model-adapters/</p><p>• vision-analyzer/</p><p>• design-intent-engine/</p><p>• patch-proposer/</p><p>• schema-validator/</p><p>• prompt-registry/</p><p>• ai-evaluation-cache/</p><p>• human-review-queue/</p><p><strong>12A.7 Phase 4 exit criteria</strong></p><p>• AI is invoked only for logged unresolved cases.</p><p>• All model outputs pass schema validation.</p><p>• No accepted AI patch bypasses Chromium measurement or rollback.</p><p>• AI improves the deterministic baseline without reducing robustness.</p><p>• Fidelity and robustness are reported separately with model, prompt, and patch provenance.</p><p><strong>12B. Updated product principle</strong></p><p>The product is not an LLM wrapper. Its moat is the measurable reverse-engineering engine: Design IR, persistent node identity, relative geometry, controlled Chromium rendering, visual comparison, bounded search, responsive validation, and reversible patches. Models are interchangeable reasoning modules behind a strict implementation contract.</p><p><strong>13. Sourcing &amp; third-party reference policy</strong></p><p>Purpose: several third-party tools and protocols (Figma MCP servers, existing Figma-to-HTML plugins, production design-to-code products) can accelerate specific packages below. This section defines exactly what may be reused, in what role, and under what constraint — so third-party code never quietly weakens the determinism guarantees in §8 or the AI containment rules in §12A.</p><p><strong>13.1 Figma MCP servers (official or open-source) — Phase 1 data source only</strong></p><p>Either the official Figma MCP server or a vetted open-source implementation may be used inside figma-client to fetch richer Figma data (variables, component/instance relationships, layout metadata) than the plain REST API exposes. This can improve the inputs to design-ir (§4.2, §4.3) but does not change the contract: every value pulled via MCP is still untrusted input that must pass through the Reference Rendering Contract (§4.1) and Chromium comparison before it affects a score.</p><p>If an open-source MCP implementation is forked, pin it to an exact commit hash and record that hash as part of the determinism inputs in §8 ("generator version"). Do not track a moving fork — an unannounced upstream change must not silently alter output for the same input.</p><p><strong>13.2 Figma MCP in Phase 4 — evidence-only, not raw file access</strong></p><p>MCP must not be used to give AI models open-ended access to the live Figma file during escalation. This would reintroduce "AI as primary interpreter," which §12A.1 and the unresolved-case taxonomy (§9) explicitly rule out. Instead, when a case is escalated, the ai-router passes only the frozen evidence for that specific case: the relevant NodeIdentity, relative-geometry diff, and screenshot crop. MCP-sourced Figma context may be used to pre-populate that evidence during Phase 1 extraction, not injected live into a Phase 4 prompt.</p><p><strong>13.3 Existing Figma-to-HTML plugins (e.g. 10xHTML) — benchmark baseline only, not generator logic</strong></p><p>Third-party Figma-to-HTML output may be used as a benchmark baseline: run it against the same benchmark frames (§4, §18) and report its fidelity/robustness scores alongside this engine's own, to demonstrate the deterministic pipeline's contribution. Its generation logic must not be forked into code-generator. That package's output is derived solely from design-ir per the mutation-boundary and patch-rollback contracts (§5.1, §5.2); importing a third party's independent heuristics would introduce an unaudited, non-reproducible component into a system whose core claim is deterministic and debuggable output.</p><p><strong>13.4 Production design-to-code tools (e.g. Builder.io Visual Copilot, Figma Make) — architecture study only</strong></p><p>Their published architecture, workflow, and stated approach to layout solving may inform the design of layout-solver (Phase 3) and design-intent-engine (Phase 4) as reference material. No code or proprietary model output from these products may be copied into this codebase. Where their approach conflicts with a lock-in rule in this PRD (§1) — for example, treating AI as the primary generator rather than a controlled escalation layer — this PRD's rule wins.</p><p><strong>13.5 General reuse rule</strong></p><p>Any third-party code, prompt template, or protocol client adopted under §13.1–§13.4 is versioned and pinned exactly like an internal package (§8). If it cannot be pinned to a specific, reproducible version, it may be used for research and architecture reference, but not compiled into a shipped package.</p><p><strong>14. Final Implementation Contracts</strong></p><p>Purpose. This section converts the architecture into concrete engineering contracts. Any behavior not explicitly changed by a later Architecture Decision Record (ADR) is governed by these contracts. Implementation teams must not invent incompatible behavior inside individual packages.</p><p><strong>14.1 Input / Output contract</strong></p><p>Input manifest</p><p>{</p><p>  "figmaFile": "file-key-or-url",</p><p>  "nodeId": "123:456",</p><p>  "benchmarkId": "dashboard-01",</p><p>  "referenceArtifact": "benchmark/reference-artifacts/dashboard-01.json",</p><p>  "config": "engine.yaml"</p><p>}</p><p>Output layout</p><p>output/&lt;runId&gt;/</p><p>  source/</p><p>  ir/design-ir.json</p><p>  generated/index.html</p><p>  generated/styles.css</p><p>  generated/assets/</p><p>  renders/&lt;viewport&gt;.png</p><p>  diffs/&lt;viewport&gt;.png</p><p>  reports/run.json</p><p>  reports/patches.jsonl</p><p>  reports/unresolved.jsonl</p><p>  manifest.json</p><p>A successful run is immutable after completion. Every output file is content-addressed or associated with the run manifest, and the manifest records all source, environment, configuration, rule, and artifact hashes required for reproducibility.</p><p><strong>14.2 Canonical NodeIR schema</strong></p><p>type NodeType =</p><p>  | "DOCUMENT" | "PAGE" | "FRAME" | "GROUP" | "RECTANGLE" | "ELLIPSE"</p><p>  | "TEXT" | "VECTOR" | "BOOLEAN" | "IMAGE" | "COMPONENT"</p><p>  | "INSTANCE" | "SECTION";</p><p>interface NodeIdentity {</p><p>  figmaId: string;</p><p>  internalId: string;</p><p>  structureHash: string;</p><p>}</p><p>interface Rect { x:number; y:number; width:number; height:number; }</p><p>interface RelativeRect { x:number; y:number; width:number; height:number; }</p><p>interface NodeIR {</p><p>  identity: NodeIdentity;</p><p>  type: NodeType;</p><p>  name: string;</p><p>  parentId: string | null;</p><p>  children: string[];</p><p>  absolute: Rect;</p><p>  relative: RelativeRect;</p><p>  visible: boolean;</p><p>  opacity: number;</p><p>  layout: LayoutIR;</p><p>  typography?: TypographyIR;</p><p>  fills?: FillIR[];</p><p>  strokes?: StrokeIR[];</p><p>  effects?: EffectIR[];</p><p>  radius?: RadiusIR;</p><p>  asset?: AssetReference;</p><p>  component?: ComponentMetadata;</p><p>  source: SourceMetadata;</p><p>}</p><p>Canonical units are CSS pixels for geometry and dimensions, normalized RGBA for colors, 0–1 for opacity, and explicit font-family/weight/style tuples for typography. No package may silently reinterpret units.</p><p>interface TransformIR {<br />  rotation?: number;<br />  matrix?: [number,number,number,number,number,number];<br />  origin?: { x:number; y:number };<br />}<br /><br />interface ConstraintIR {<br />  horizontal: "LEFT" | "RIGHT" | "CENTER" | "LEFT_RIGHT" | "SCALE" | "STRETCH" | "NONE";<br />  vertical: "TOP" | "BOTTOM" | "CENTER" | "TOP_BOTTOM" | "SCALE" | "STRETCH" | "NONE";<br />}<br /><br />Rule: transforms and Figma constraints are canonical source data. Their browser representation must preserve observed rotation/transform and anchoring semantics across required breakpoints. Unsupported semantics become explicit unresolved cases rather than arbitrary positioning.</p><p><strong>14.3 LayoutIR schema</strong></p><p>interface LayoutIR {</p><p>  mode: "NONE" | "AUTO_LAYOUT" | "GRID_LIKE" | "ABSOLUTE";</p><p>  axis?: "HORIZONTAL" | "VERTICAL";</p><p>  gap?: number;</p><p>  padding?: { top:number; right:number; bottom:number; left:number };</p><p>  align?: "START" | "CENTER" | "END" | "STRETCH";</p><p>  justify?: "START" | "CENTER" | "END" | "SPACE_BETWEEN";</p><p>  sizing?: { width:"FIXED"|"HUG"|"FILL"; height:"FIXED"|"HUG"|"FILL" };</p><p>  wrap?: boolean;</p><p>  minWidth?: number;</p><p>  maxWidth?: number;</p><p>  minHeight?: number;</p><p>  maxHeight?: number;</p><p>  aspectRatio?: number;</p><p>}</p><p><strong>14.4 Figma extraction contract</strong></p><p>Authentication is supplied through a secret outside source control. Tokens are never persisted in IR, logs, benchmark artifacts, or generated code.</p><p>Extractor recursively traverses the selected frame and preserves stable Figma IDs, component/instance metadata, paint/style data, layout data, text data, and asset references.</p><p>Every external asset is downloaded, hashed, validated, and mapped to a deterministic local asset path before code generation.</p><p>Extraction is versioned by parser version and Figma source version. A parser upgrade changes generator provenance and invalidates prior reproducibility claims.</p><p>Rate limits and transient API failures use bounded retries with exponential backoff. Permanent failures terminate the run with a typed error code.</p><p><strong>14.5 Figma feature support policy</strong></p><table><thead><tr><th><p><strong>Feature</strong></p></th><th><p><strong>Phase 1–3</strong></p></th><th><p><strong>Policy</strong></p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Frame / Group / Auto Layout</p></th><th><p>YES</p></th><th><p>Deterministically mapped to semantic HTML/CSS</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Text</p></th><th><p>YES</p></th><th><p>Exact font readiness required; missing font is a hard benchmark failure</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Image fills</p></th><th><p>YES</p></th><th><p>Downloaded and hashed; deterministic local asset path</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Component / Instance</p></th><th><p>YES metadata</p></th><th><p>Identity preserved; abstraction inference deferred to Phase 4</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Vector / Boolean</p></th><th><p>LIMITED</p></th><th><p>Supported when export/render path is deterministic; otherwise unresolved asset/rendering</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Effects / shadows</p></th><th><p>YES basic</p></th><th><p>Only representable CSS effects are emitted</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Prototype descendants.</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>Transforms / rotation</p></td><td><p>YES / LIMITED</p></td><td><p>TransformIR preserves rotation/matrix/origin; arbitrary transforms are forbidden as screenshot fixes.</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>Figma constraints</p></td><td><p>YES / LIMITED</p></td><td><p>ConstraintIR models responsive anchoring/scale/stretch behavior and is validated across required breakpoints.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><p><strong>14.6 Figma → HTML/CSS mapping rules</strong></p><table><thead><tr><th><p><strong>Observed intent</strong></p></th><th><p><strong>Default implementation</strong></p></th><th><p><strong>Escalation condition</strong></p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Horizontal Auto Layout</p></th><th><p>flex row</p></th><th><p>Only if evidence indicates grid/other structure</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Vertical Auto Layout</p></th><th><p>flex column</p></th><th><p>Only if evidence indicates grid/other structure</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Auto Layout gap</p></th><th><p>gap</p></th><th><p>Never emulate with arbitrary transforms</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Padding</p></th><th><p>padding</p></th><th><p>Use side-specific values when asymmetric</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Hug contents</p></th><th><p>auto intrinsic sizing</p></th><th><p>Fallback only with measured evidence</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Fill container</p></th><th><p>flex:1 / width:100% depending on axis</p></th><th><p>Must preserve measured geometry</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Fixed size</p></th><th><p>fixed px dimensions</p></th><th><p>Candidate solver may relax only within
